Faculty Senate Executive Committee Bill #2025-2026-05 December 11, 2025 Faculty Senate Meeting Rationale: Students can currently repeat a course once without seeking permission.
Although the language of the pertinent statute (s8.33.31) states that permission of an academic dean is required for repeating a class a third -- and perhaps fourth, fifth, etc. -- time, this cannot be coded in ecampus as a block to registration until the academic dean approves.
Per discussions with Jack Humphrey, adding the requirement of *may be repeated a third time only in exceptional circumstances and only with authorization of the dean of the college in which the student is enrolled.' to s8.33.31 would require students to get approval from the dean of their college.
UConn: "The student may take the course a third time with the permission of the dean of the school or college in which the student is enrolled and the instructor of the course.

Under no circumstances may a student take a course more than three times." UVM: "A standard course may be repeated more than one time only at the discretion of the dean of the student's college/school, after consideration of any impact on the student's financial aid and/or progress to graduation." UMass Dartmouth: "lf students attempt to enroll in the same course for the third time, our SIS does not allow them to enroll.
They must complete a third or more attempt paper form (see attached) and receive approval from their college dean's office.
The third or more attempt form is UMass Amherst: “...[students] can only repeat the course once unless a dean gives them permission for a third attempt (or the course is coded as repeatable for credit).
This method requires a lot less intervention by advisors, deans and Registrar's Office staff." URIDATA Between fall 2021 and summer 2025, there were 27,296 second attempts of a graded course; 2,260 third attempts; and 402 fourth attempts.

Online -Academic Year No Initiation Date First Degree Date Spring 2026 Fall 2027 Program Description @ The Graduate Certificate in the Foundations of Science Communication is designed for individuals who seek to deepen their understanding of the principles and conceptual frameworks underpinning effective science communication. This program explores the interdisciplinary theories that inform how scientific knowledge is disseminated, perceived, and used by diverse audiences. Students will engage with topics such as message framing, perception, and persuasion; political ideologies, identity politics, and policymaking; disability studies and accessible design; health communication; and the ethics of public engagement with science. Students will develop a critical lens to analyze the impact of communication strategies on societal trust in science and policy decision-making. This certificate will prepare students to excel as science and health communicators, advocates, and policy advisors. This certificate complements the Graduate Certificate in thePractices of Science Communication, serving as a pathway to the stackable Master of Arts in Applied Science Communication, Program requirements: - WRT534(NRS540) -COM525(MAF525) -WRT565 - One of the following: C0M460, COM455, COM523, COM522(MAF522), NRS509, PHL533, HLT504, HLT505, HLT506
